data_management.access: Public outputs contain only redistributable or sufficiently derived material; restricted inputs are access-controlled and excluded.
data_management.public_outputs: Protocol, code, schemas, provenance, aggregate findings, and rights-cleared derived datasets only.
data_management.retention: Retain immutable protocol releases, manifests, checksums, amendment history, and deviation records with repository history.
data_management.storage: Version-controlled contracts, schemas, lawful fixtures, and derived metadata; source payloads remain under source-specific controls.

ethics.review_statement: Institutional ethics applicability and final public wording require maintainer confirmation before external submission.
ethics.risk_statement: The study uses medicine administrative records and no individual participant data; principal risks are misinterpretation, source-rights breach, and overstated coverage.

registration_responses.analysis_plan: Use the committed Phase 2 analysis plan, report denominators and unknowns, and label any unplanned analysis exploratory.
registration_responses.design: Repeated cross-jurisdiction status comparisons using bitemporal assertions and M-090 validity states.
registration_responses.hypotheses: No confirmatory hypothesis tests or causal hypotheses are preregistered; analyses are descriptive.
registration_responses.sampling_plan: The denominator is the versioned source census and eligibility rules in the academic protocol, not an inferred global universe.
registration_responses.stopping_rule: Freeze the preregistered source census and software identities at approved registration; later additions are prospective amendments.
registration_responses.study_type: Observational, descriptive, secondary analysis of governed public administrative medicine sources.
registration_responses.variables: Regulatory and funding status are separate outcomes; entity, indication, population, time, mapping, provenance, and uncertainty qualify each comparison.

research_questions: How does source-supported regulatory status vary for comparable medicine entities across included jurisdictions and times?
How does source-supported public funding status vary independently for those comparable entities across included jurisdictions and times?
How do source coverage, mapping validity, missingness, and conflicts affect those descriptive comparisons?
summary: A prospective, descriptive study of source-supported medicine regulatory and public-funding status across jurisdictions, with explicit comparison validity, provenance, coverage, uncertainty, and rights boundaries.
title: Global Medicines Atlas: prospective protocol for regulatory approval and public funding comparisons
